question.worked_solution:
The denominator is $1-3\text{i}$ and its conjugate is $1+3\text{i}.$ We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $1+3\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{2\text{i}}{1-3\text{i}} & =\frac{2\text{i}}{1-3\text{i}}\cdot \frac{1+3\text{i}}{1+3\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{2\text{i}+6{\text{i}}^{2}}{{1}^{2}-{3}^{2}{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{6(-1)+2\text{i}}{{1}^{2}+{3}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-6+2\text{i}}{1+9} \\  & =\frac{-6+2\text{i}}{10}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{-6+2\text{i}}{10}=-\frac{6}{10}+\frac{2}{10}\text{i}=-\frac{3}{5}+\frac{1}{5}\text{i}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
